    the short guide

    How to make an IMAT study plan that works

    A good IMAT study plan answers three questions: how many weeks you have, how many hours you can really study, and which sections cost you the most points. The planner above does the maths for you, and this is the thinking behind it.

    1. Start your IMAT study plan from the exam date

    Count backwards from exam day. Leave the final days light, put your full mocks in the last weeks, and spread the syllabus over the weeks before them. The earlier you start, the more slowly you can cover each topic.

    2. Match the hours to the exam

    The IMAT has 60 questions, and Biology and Chemistry carry the most. A balanced IMAT study plan gives each section time in proportion to its questions, then adds extra hours where you feel weak.

    3. Learn, practise, then test under time

    Go through each topic three times: learn it, practise it with questions, then review it fast. Add short spaced reviews so earlier topics do not fade while you move on.

    4. Put timed mocks and review days in your IMAT study plan

    Do full 100-minute mocks under exam conditions and keep a day to go through every mistake. Mocks show you where your IMAT study plan needs to change.

    5. Keep the plan realistic

    Choose study days you can keep, take rest days and holidays off, and rebuild your IMAT study plan from today if you fall behind. A plan you follow beats a perfect plan you drop.

    6. Pair it with the syllabus and books

    Use the syllabus checklist and recommended books on this page to see what each week of your IMAT study plan should cover. Then use the planner above to schedule it.

    why it works

    How this IMAT study plan is built

    Many IMAT study plans are just a list of chapters. This IMAT study plan follows methods that learning research supports.

    Weighted to the real exam

    Hours follow the IMAT's 60 questions: Biology 23, Chemistry 15, Physics & Maths 13, Logic 5, Reading & GK 4. Physics & Maths follow Locomotive's topic map with baseline hours per topic (101h + 89h). Weak sections get extra practice.

    Spaced repetition

    When you finish a topic, it comes back for short reviews after 1, 4, 11 and 25 days. Spacing reviews out is one of the most reliable ways to remember more.

    Active recall, not re-reading

    Every learning session ends with a closed-book summary, flashcards and questions. Testing yourself builds memory far more than highlighting.

    Interleaving

    Subjects alternate through the day and practice sets are shuffled. You learn to spot the question type, just like in the exam.

    Mocks with autopsy days

    Full 100-minute mocks under exam conditions, each followed by a review day. Every error is tagged and fixed. The mock alone is only half the value.

    Pace you can sustain

    Fixed focus sessions with breaks, your own study days and public holidays off, weekly check-ins and a lighter last few days so you arrive rested.

    good questions

    Questions

    How many hours a day should I study for the IMAT?

    It depends on how much time you have. With 6+ months, 3-4 focused hours on weekdays is enough for most students starting from scratch. With 2-3 months, plan on 5-7 hours. Focused hours matter more than hours at the desk. Choose a number you can really keep up, and change it here at any time.

    What should an IMAT study plan include?

    A good IMAT study plan covers the whole syllabus, gives each section time in proportion to its questions, schedules spaced reviews, and includes timed mock exams with a review day after each one. This IMAT study plan generator builds all of that from your dates and daily hours.

    How long should my IMAT study plan be?

    Your IMAT study plan runs from the start date you choose to the exam date. More weeks means a slower, lighter plan. Fewer weeks means a faster plan that leans on revision and mocks. Enter your real dates and the planner sets the pace for you.

    Is this IMAT study plan free?

    Yes. The IMAT study plan generator is free and needs no sign-up. You can download your IMAT study plan as a PDF, spreadsheet or calendar file.

    Where does the syllabus come from?

    It is the Locomotive IMAT 2027 syllabus, which expands the official MUR specifications into a checklist of main topics and subtopics. MUR usually publishes the new decree only 1 to 2 months before the exam, and it rarely changes much, so the list lets you start early. Topics marked * are named in the official decree but not spelled out in our list.

    Why go through every topic 3 times?

    One read-through makes a topic feel familiar, but you cannot yet recall it or use it under pressure. Pass 1 builds understanding, pass 2 turns it into correct answers, and pass 3 makes it fast and reliable under exam conditions. Short spaced reviews after 1, 4, 11 and 25 days keep each topic fresh between the passes.

    What do I need to follow this plan?

    Your textbook or course notes for each topic, flashcards (paper or an app), a notebook for your error log, and IMAT-style questions: official past papers plus a bank of mocks. Older official papers (before 2023) use a different question split, so use them by section.

    What if I fall behind?

    Don't try to cram the missed days. Press "Rebuild from today" above your plan. Topics whose learning sessions you have all ticked are skipped, and your reviews and mocks are rescheduled around the time you have left.

    Can I open my plan on another device?

    Yes. Press "Copy link to this plan" and open the link on your phone or laptop. The link rebuilds the same plan. Ticks and mock scores stay on the device where you entered them.

    What happens on a "Mock autopsy" day?

    You go through every wrong, blank and guessed question from yesterday's mock. You tag the reason (knowledge gap, misread, calculation slip, time pressure, bad guess), redo each one closed-book, and turn the gaps into repair sessions. This is where most of your score improvement comes from.

    Will my ticked sessions be saved?

    Ticks are saved in this browser only. For a permanent copy, download the PDF or the spreadsheet and track your progress there.
